meta.purpose: Parameterize Lucy autobiographical retrieval from human memory science — not keyword TF toys.
meta.not_clinical: This is character continuity engineering inspired by peer-reviewed models; not a PTSD diagnosis tool.

papers.cite: Conway & Pleydell-Pearce (2000). The construction of autobiographical memories in the self-memory system. Psychological Review.
papers.use: SMS hierarchy; generative (goal-directed) vs direct (cue-driven) retrieval; current goals gate what reaches consciousness.

papers.cite: Tulving & Thomson (1973). Encoding specificity and retrieval processes in episodic memory. Psychological Review.
papers.use: Retrieval probability rises with overlap between retrieval cues and features stored at encoding.

papers.cite: Berntsen (2010/2021). Involuntary autobiographical memories; cue distinctiveness & cue overload.
papers.use: Direct/involuntary path: distinctive feature overlap wins; cues shared by many events are weak (cue overload).

papers.cite: Brewin et al. (1996/2010/2014). Dual representation theory of PTSD (SAM/VAM; S-rep/C-rep).
papers.use: Trauma: strong situationally accessible sensory-affective traces + weak contextual/verbal links → cue-triggered intrusion; recovery = re-associate into contextual autobiographical memory.

papers.cite: Ehlers & Clark (2000). A cognitive model of PTSD. Behaviour Research and Therapy.
papers.use: Poor elaboration into AM base → weak intentional recall, strong associative/perceptual triggering, here-and-now threat sense; appraisals maintain current threat.

papers.cite: Anderson (2003). Rethinking interference: inhibitory control & retrieval-induced forgetting.
papers.use: Spreading activation to competitors; inhibitory control suppresses non-selected associates after retrieval.

papers.cite: Roberts & Mroczek (2008). Personality trait change in adulthood.
papers.use: Traits/motives keep changing via life experience — event ledger growth.
